newsitem.title: INDIA: India's parliament mourns Deng in silence.
newsitem.headline: India's parliament mourns Deng in silence.

text.p: India's parliament marked the death of Deng Xiaoping with a minute of silence on Friday after its speaker praised the Chinese leader's contribution to strengthening bilateral ties between the Asian giants.
"Deng Xiaoping was a great leader of the Chinese people whose contribution to the modernisation of China will be ever remembered," speaker P.A. Sangma told the Lok Sabha, or lower house.

Sangma recalled Deng's meeting in 1988 with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, which was sealed by a long handshake that symbolised warming relations and ended years of suspicion following a brief border war in 1962.

"In mourning the demise of Deng Xiaoping, we reaffirm our desire to build friendly, good neighbourly, constructive and cooperative relations with China for the prosperity of our two peoples," Sangma said before asking members to stand and observe a minute of silence.
China claims some 90,000 sq km (35,000 sq miles) in India's northeastern Arunachal Pradesh state. China also regards India's northern Sikkim state as disputed.
India says China occupies about 33,000 sq km (13,000 sq miles) in the Aksai Chin region of its northern Jammu and Kashmir state.
